label: Q3 2026
headline: AI orders are still accelerating, but the market has started paying a lower multiple

points.t: Wafer shipments grew only 9.6% in a year while revenue grew 41%; the difference comes from more advanced, more expensive nodes.
HPC is 68% of revenue, +22% q/q; smartphones were roughly flat y/y.

points.b: Guidance raised twice in a year
points.t: Full-year growth went from about 30% to about 44%, and capex was raised to $60–64B.

reaction: Stock: closed −1.8% on report day and fell another 2.3% the next day. Taiwan's chip stocks had already sold off sharply the day before the report. Profits are being delivered; the worry is how long the peak lasts and how large capex gets in the next two years, so the multiple was compressed (see Valuation).

volprice.title: Revenue = wafer shipments × revenue per wafer
volprice.take: More than 70% of TSMC's growth this year came from price. Shipments rose only modestly; customers are paying for pricier nodes such as 2nm and 3nm.
volprice.note: Revenue per wafer = total revenue ÷ 12-inch-equivalent wafer shipments. Total revenue includes advanced packaging and other non-wafer revenue, so this is approximate. Quarter on quarter: shipments +3.2%, revenue per wafer +12.6%.

segments.title: By platform
segments.take: Of the $13.6B of added revenue in a year, 95% came from HPC (AI accelerators, server CPUs, etc.). Smartphones were once 30%; now only 20%.

rows.why: AI accelerators, server CPUs and networking chips. 57% of revenue a year ago, 68% now.
A seasonal q/q rebound, roughly flat y/y. Management also mentioned pressure on consumer demand.

segments.note: Platform amounts are estimated from the company's percentage shares times total revenue; shares are whole numbers, so small platforms carry larger errors. Quarter-on-quarter growth is as reported by the company.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: TSMC is the common factory for every chip in this chain: NVIDIA GPUs, Google TPUs and Amazon Trainium are all made here. However customers compete with each other, TSMC gets paid; its risk is the whole chain's capex slowing at once.

items.w: AI accelerators, server CPUs and networking chips are 68% of revenue, versus 57% a year ago. Amazon's CEO said in late October that “everybody is producing their advanced chips with the same provider”; each gets an allocation and decides how much to sell versus use.
Shipments grew only 9.6% in a year while revenue grew 41%; customers pay more for 2nm and 3nm.

In the late-October reporting season, Google's capex was 121% of operating cash flow and Amazon's 179%, with more than $250B of outside financing between them this year. TSMC's orders sit upstream of that spending.

Management said consumer and price-sensitive products are “facing challenges”; in the same period Sandisk's consumer business fell 29% q/q and Intel cut guidance on PCs, as higher memory prices squeeze consumer electronics.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: TSMC is already far ahead of its long-term targets; the variables are what price the doubled 2nm capacity sells at and how much overseas fabs drag on margins.

items.w: 2nm-family capacity more than doubles in 2027; the new Tainan 3nm fab enters volume production in 1H 2027 and Arizona fab 2 in Q3 2027.
The CFO only said pricing is “very strategic”; CoWoS advanced packaging is still customers' first choice.
A14 risk production in 2027 and volume production in 2028; Japan fab 2 produces 3nm from 2028.

Long-term targets: revenue growth approaching 25% a year over 2024–2029, AI accelerators growing in the mid-to-high 50s percent, and gross margin of 56% or higher through the cycle. This year's growth is about 44% with a 66% gross margin, both above target; management says AI accelerator growth “could be higher”.
Watch whether Q4 capex falls well below $19B because customers delay, HPC q/q growth below 10% for two quarters, gross margin below 65%, and the overseas-fab drag widening to 3–4 points.

extras.title: By node
extras.take: 3nm and 2nm together are now 41% of wafer revenue, versus 23% a year ago. The most advanced nodes sell at the highest prices but dilute margins early in the ramp.

items.w: The main reason gross margin fell 1.3 points q/q. 2nm capacity more than doubles again in 2027, so dilution continues near term.
US and Japan fabs cost more. Management expects about a 2-point drag near term, widening to 3–4 points in the later years of the five-year period.
Priced in US dollars, reported in NT dollars. Q4 guidance assumes NT$31.8 per US$, slightly stronger than Q3's actual 31.98, a slight negative for gross margin.

trends.why: Up 7 points in a year; slightly lower this quarter on 2nm
Expenses growing far slower than revenue

valuation.take: On full-year 2026 earnings (including Q4 guidance), the P/E is about 24x; at the five-year median multiple, the current price needs only about 13% growth next year, below our bear case. The valuation is mainly supported by profits already earned.

forward.title: Full-year earnings from company guidance
steps: Q4 revenue at the guided midpoint of $53.3B, NT$1.69T at the guided rate of 31.8
Operating margin at the guided midpoint of 57.5% → operating income about NT$975B
Non-operating items and tax at Q3's ratio (net income ÷ operating income = 0.87) → net income about NT$849B
Q4 EPS about NT$32.7, about $5.15 per ADR
forward.note: Q4 annualized, the P/E is about 20x. Our estimate, not a company forecast.

scenarios.note: Margin is the operating margin. Base is full-year 2026 revenue of about $176B. *Price: if the market pays the five-year median of 22.4x, the $418.51 price needs 2027 EPS of $18.68, about 13% revenue growth. That means the price is already near the bear case; if the market thinks growth has peaked, the multiple could stay below the median. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

history.title: Against its own last 5 years
history.note: About 28x now, above 19 of the last 20 quarter ends, the 95th percentile; median about 22x. Only the end of June this year was higher. StockAnalysis data, slightly different from the 26.9x above mainly because of currency and share-count methods.

decomp.title: The −1.8% post-report move, decomposed
head: TTM earnings
P/E
decomp.note: Trailing EPS jumped 12% in one go, yet the stock didn't rise, meaning the market cut the multiple from 31x to 27x. It is the opposite of TSLA, where profits fell and the multiple rose.

cash.title: Capex intensity
cash.note: Of every $100 of revenue, about $30 goes back into fabs, yet free cash flow stays positive. The full-year capex guide of $60–64B with $40.6B spent in three quarters means $19–23B in Q4, a quarterly record. Management said 2026–2028 investment will be “meaningfully higher”.

calc: 1 ADR = 5 common shares; about 25.93B common shares → about 5.19B ADR equivalents → market cap about $2,170B
Free cash flow is reported in NT dollars (NT$1,480.7B), about $46.9B at each quarter's average rate
Scenario EPS = 2027 revenue × operating margin × 0.87 ÷ 5.19B ADRs
Scenario-implied price = scenario EPS/ADR × the five-year median P/E of 22.4x; room = implied price ÷ $418.51 − 1

pricezone.sub: 2027 EPS/ADR (scenarios above) × our P/E; price at the 29 Oct close
pricezone.why: The price is above the zone: buying now, the base case gains about 10% while the bear case loses about 26%, a reward/risk of about 0.4. Near the $365 midpoint the reward/risk is about 2.3, and the low end is close to the bear-case price. The base case uses the five-year median P/E of 22.4x; the bear case uses 18x because the multiple tends to fall first when the market fears the AI investment cycle has peaked.

changes.before: No new number, only that demand is stronger than expected.
changes.now: Kept the original guide (mid-to-high 50s% CAGR for 2024–2029), but said it “could be higher”.
About 2 points near term, 3–4 points in the later years of the five-year period.
Consumer and price-sensitive products are “facing challenges”; 2027 planning will be prudent.
Evaluating Texas and discussing sites tied to the Terafab project, stressing TSMC must operate them.

items: “There is no ceiling on TSMC's profitability”, but it won't jump overnight
About 20 fabs under construction worldwide; CoWoS advanced packaging is still customers' first choice
How much capacity grows next year: the CFO said it's “too early”
Whether 2027 supply stays tight: can't say, because demand is still rising
Whether price increases apply to existing contracts: only that pricing is “very strategic”
Whether gross margin holds 65% as 2nm's share rises
Monthly revenue reported around the 10th of each month
Q4 capex clearly below $19B because customers delayed, not because of lead times
HPC q/q growth below 10% for two straight quarters
Gross margin below the 65% low end of guidance

insider.title: TSMC does not file US Form 4s
insider.text: TSMC is a foreign private issuer; the SEC does not require its directors and officers to file Form 4. Insider holdings changes are reported on the Taiwan Stock Exchange's Market Observation Post System, which would need a separate data source.
